mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the reactions of metals with water?

options.A: All metals react vigorously with cold water.
options.B: Alkali metals react vigorously with cold water, alkaline earth metals react with steam, and most other metals do not react with water.
options.C: Only transition metals react with water.
options.D: Alkali earth metals react with cold water, while alkali metals do not react.

mcqs.answer: Alkali metals react vigorously with cold water, alkaline earth metals react with steam, and most other metals do not react with water.
mcqs.explanation: Alkali metals (e.g., Na, K) react violently with cold water. Alkaline earth metals (e.g., Mg, Ca) react only with hot water/steam. Most other metals such as Fe, Cu do not react with water at room temperature. Hence option B accurately distinguishes the reactivity patterns.

mcqs.question: Which metal among the following does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
mcqs.explanation: Copper is placed below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Zinc, iron and magnesium are above hydrogen and therefore react, liberating H₂ gas.

mcqs.question: When metal X is added to dilute HCl, hydrogen gas is evolved. When metal Y is added to the same acid, no visible reaction occurs. Which statement is true regarding their positions in the reactivity series?

options.A: Metal X is higher (more reactive) than metal Y.
options.B: Metal Y is higher (more reactive) than metal X.
options.D: Reactivity cannot be inferred from this observation.

mcqs.answer: Metal X is higher (more reactive) than metal Y.
mcqs.explanation: A metal that displaces hydrogen from an acid is above hydrogen in the reactivity series. Since metal X does this and metal Y does not, metal X must be more reactive than metal Y. Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: A metal does not react with water but reacts readily with dilute HCl to produce hydrogen gas. Which metal could it be?
mcqs.explanation: Iron does not react with cold water, but it does react with dilute acids, displacing hydrogen. Sodium reacts violently with water, magnesium reacts with steam, and aluminium forms a protective oxide layer that hinders reaction with water but still reacts with acid; iron is the best match for the described behaviour.

mcqs.question: Identify the correct statement about metal reactions with water.

options.A: All metals react with water to produce hydrogen.
options.B: Only alkali metals react vigorously with cold water, while other metals either react with steam or not at all.
options.C: No metal reacts with water under any condition.
options.D: Only transition metals react with water.

mcqs.answer: Only alkali metals react vigorously with cold water, while other metals either react with steam or not at all.
mcqs.explanation: The common misconception is that every metal reacts with water. In reality, only alkali metals react vigorously with cold water; alkaline earth metals need steam; many metals (e.g., Fe, Cu) do not react with water at ordinary temperatures. Option B correctly reflects this.

mcqs.question: Why does zinc react with dilute HCl whereas copper does not?

options.A: Zinc is placed higher than copper in the reactivity series.
options.B: Copper is placed higher than zinc in the reactivity series.
options.C: Both metals have the same reactivity.
options.D: The reaction depends on the melting point of the metal.

mcqs.answer: Zinc is placed higher than copper in the reactivity series.
mcqs.explanation: In the reactivity series, zinc lies above hydrogen and copper lies below hydrogen. Therefore zinc can displace hydrogen from dilute HCl, while copper cannot. The melting point is irrelevant to this acid‑metal reaction.

mcqs.question: Magnesium and aluminium are both placed in dilute HCl. Which metal will evolve hydrogen gas more rapidly?

options.C: Both evolve hydrogen at the same rate
options.D: The rate cannot be predicted from the reactivity series

mcqs.explanation: Magnesium is higher than aluminium in the reactivity series, meaning it is more reactive and displaces hydrogen more readily. Consequently, magnesium reacts faster with dilute HCl, producing hydrogen at a higher rate.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions will NOT occur spontaneously under standard conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Zinc, iron and magnesium are above hydrogen and do react, releasing H₂ gas. Therefore option C is the reaction that will not occur spontaneously.
